comparison: Both strongly support the adaptation findings (C6-C7, C41-C43, C56-C63). OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and cross-species consistency. Peer reviewers describe the data as 'convincing' with 'sound methods,' accepting the findings without challenge. OpenEval also includes C47 (cross-species validation) which peer review explicitly addresses.

Both support directional decoding findings (C9, C44, C101, C103-C105, C108-C110). OpenEval finds the prediction accuracy and model analysis convincing. Peer reviewers accept this as a key finding, with the editor noting it 'demonstrates convincingly' an alternative to traditional models. Both recognize the importance of directional cells for predicting perception.

Both address the minimal distance hypothesis (C10, C74) and repulsive effects (C75, C79-C80, C82). OpenEval finds strong evidence against the hypothesis. Peer reviewers strongly endorse this negative result, with Reviewer 1 calling it 'very convincing' and the editor noting it 'demonstrates convincingly' the failure of traditional models.

Both address the main conclusion (C12-C13). OpenEval finds it well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY about broader implications, with concerns about what readers should take away and whether the study makes predictions about downstream readout. This represents a key disagreement on the strength of the overall conclusion.

Perfect overlap on neural heterogeneity characterization (C64-C70). OpenEval finds the characterization well-documented and important for understanding population responses. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as part of the careful experimental design, though they don't discuss them specifically.

Both address the model's explanatory power (C11, C48-C50) and mechanistic details (C93-C97, C100, C106-C107, C144). OpenEval finds the model successfully integrates observations. Peer reviewers accept the modeling as 'rigorous' and 'sound' but note uncertainty about whether it represents the actual mechanism (observational vs interventional study).

Both evaluate the mechanistic model (C89-C100, C144-C146). OpenEval emphasizes the model is well-constrained and tested against alternatives. Peer reviewers accept the modeling results as valid and rigorous, though they express caution about definitive mechanistic identification due to the observational nature of the study.

Both address decoding analyses showing repulsive effects (C75-C88). OpenEval emphasizes the high statistical significance (p<10^-43) and consistency across methods. Peer reviewers accept the decoding methodology as rigorous, with consistency across methods strengthening conclusions.

Both address methodological details (C51-C54, C111-C128). OpenEval finds methods well-documented with appropriate technical details for reproducibility. Peer reviewers accept the methodology, stating 'experimental design and data collection appear to have been executed carefully' and 'methods seem sound,' with only a minor suggestion to include more methods detail in results.

Both address stimulus design and psychophysical properties (C129-C138). OpenEval finds these well-documented methodological details. Peer reviewers accept the approach without specific concerns as part of the overall sound methodology.

Both address analysis methods (C139-C143). OpenEval finds the selection criteria and validation approaches appropriate. Peer reviewers accept the decoding methodology as rigorous, noting that consistency across multiple methods strengthens conclusions.

Both address technical analysis details (C148). OpenEval finds the use of multiple decoding methods and non-parametric statistics strengthens robustness. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these technical details as part of the sound methodology.

Both address model control analyses (C98-C99). OpenEval finds the model explicitly tested against alternative mechanisms. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these controls as part of the rigorous modeling approach, with systematic comparison of model variants strengthening mechanistic conclusions.

Both address technical modeling details (C145-C146). OpenEval finds the model well-constrained by data. Peer reviewers accept these technical details without comment as part of the overall sound methodology.

Both address cross-species validation (C47). OpenEval finds the parallel findings strengthen generalizability. Peer reviewers note that consistency between ferret and human data strengthens the findings.

OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1-C30) as appropriately supported by citations. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these introductory claims, focusing instead on novel findings and methodology.

Partial overlap on repulsive effects (C75, C79-C80, C82). OpenEval emphasizes the highly significant repulsive effect and temporal dynamics. Peer review R3 focuses on the negative result regarding traditional models, strongly endorsing the failure of the minimal distance hypothesis.
